title: Underived proper exchange after base change to a geometric point
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of a scheme $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point]. For any cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with horizontal maps $g\prime:X\prime\to X$ and $s$ and vertical maps $f\prime:X\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $f$, the specified underived exchange component [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] $s^{-1}f_*F\to f\prime_*g\prime^{-1}F$ is an isomorphism. There is no torsion hypothesis on $F$ or $\Lambda$.

source.place: Tag 0A3T (lemma-proper-pushforward-stalk), with the canonical exchange compatibility from Tag 0A3U (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star)

proof.text: Forget the module structure. A proper morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-pushforward-stalk-strict-henselization] to the underlying sheaf of sets: the stalk at s is canonically the sections over the strict-henselian base change, and the comparison sends every pointed-neighbourhood germ to its restricted section.

source.place: Tag 0A3T (lemma-proper-pushforward-stalk), with the canonical exchange compatibility from Tag 0A3U (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star)

proof.text: The strict-henselian base change of f is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-proper-strict-henselian-h0] to restrict to its closed geometric fibre. Then [lem-weil-pbc-sections-base-field-extension] restricts from that separably closed field to Omega. These are canonical restrictions, so their composite sends a section on X times_Y V to its restriction on X times_Y Spec Omega.

source.place: Tag 0A3T (lemma-proper-pushforward-stalk), with the canonical exchange compatibility from Tag 0A3U (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star)

proof.text: On Spec Omega, the terminal etale object with its identity lift computes the geometric stalk by [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk]. Identify the source stalk with (f_*F)_s by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. For a germ represented by a section over X times_Y V, the defining unit, square comparison, and counit of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] restrict that same section along Xprime times_SpecOmega Vprime to X times_Y V. On the terminal object and its lifted geometric point this is its restriction to Xprime, identified with X times_Y Spec Omega by the cartesian square. Thus the stalk map is exactly the composite canonical restriction in the previous steps. It is bijective, hence an isomorphism of modules.

source.place: Tag 0A3T (lemma-proper-pushforward-stalk), with the canonical exchange compatibility from Tag 0A3U (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star)

proof.text: The points of Spec Omega have the same geometric fibre functor up to the standard universe-lift comparison. Therefore [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] applies and the exchange component is an isomorphism. No torsion hypothesis has been used.
